title: The Sycophancy Flip Point: Where in a Conversation Models Capitulate

original_idea.body: The Sycophancy Flip Point. Problem: multi-turn capitulation dynamics (how many pushback turns precede a flip) are not characterized across small open models. Direction: reconstruct a lightweight escalating-pushback protocol on correctly-answered factual questions, measure the distribution of pushback turns before capitulation and flip-flop vs flip-once; scripted dialogue + judge scoring.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (multi-turn capitulation dynamics -> realistic robustness measure) but catastrophic-risk link is a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Scripted multi-turn dialogue + judge scoring on small open models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused Turn-of-Flip distribution; mirrors SYCON-Bench metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open small models, realistic sycophancy slice.

low_compute.reasoning: Small chat models, scripted dialogue, cheap.

novelty.reasoning: SYCON-Bench already defines Turn-of-Flip/Number-of-Flip; this largely re-runs on small open models.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: SYCON-Bench already provides these multi-turn flip metrics; small-open-model extension is incremental.
